# Separate failed player behavior from test and lifecycle failures

The latest player feedback concerns a retained formal world, not a fresh
generated fixture. Its second model request was interrupted during exit,
although the containing turn was marked completed. A visible promise to fix
pickup therefore cannot establish that any patch, check, or adoption happened.

Acceptance retains the original transcript, explicit SQL projections,
request settlements, formal manifest, and real saved player position. It
first reproduces the PCK behavior and then continues the same ordinary
conversation in a copy. Reports separate the real pickup failure from a long
test-root execution failure and a later pre-model TURN_ENDED rejection.

Short-profile relocation preserves prior failed evidence and generated
source, changes only the independent headless ownership marker, and avoids
blind replacement of absolute fields. Any resulting context mismatch must
be diagnosed through actual product responses rather than bypassed.

This adds diagnostic evidence, not a new product authorization or model
capability boundary. Native software callbacks never send physical input,
activate windows, request pointer lock, or use the player's live browser.
